current_episode.title: Greg Johnson - CEO at Warwick Development NW

guest.bio_context: Greg Johnson took over Warwick Development NW as MD approximately two years before this conversation, following his father's cancer diagnosis. His uncle founded the business in 1998, and his father took over in 2008 before Greg assumed leadership. Greg had undergone a 15-16 year apprenticeship learning the business before formally taking the helm, and has since led the company to win the G Awards Fabricator of the Year and other national recognitions including a Sunday Express Supplier of the Year award.

context.real_quote: We make windows and doors, but if we can use our platform as a business to give back and make a difference to our local communities, then I think that's the winning formula.

pending_qa.q: What role does government policy in house building play in window manufacturing demand?
pending_qa.r: The government earmarked 39 billion for social and affordable housing in a recent spending review, plus a couple of billion for retrofit work. Greg noted that 165,000 children are currently stuck in temporary accommodation due to insufficient housing stock, and whether built through modern methods construction or traditional methods, all houses require windows and doors, making house building growth critical to his sector.

pending_qa.q: How did podcast vulnerability about personal challenges affect industry relationships and health awareness?
pending_qa.r: After discussing his father's cancer diagnosis and emotional challenges on a previous podcast, Greg received numerous messages from industry peers, MDs, and CEOs offering congratulations and support. More meaningfully, he learned that listeners took health action based on his openness, with people reporting they attended prostate examinations after hearing him discuss his father's diagnosis, highlighting the importance of mental and physical well-being given the industry's average age of 46-47 and predominantly male composition.

pending_qa.q: What local charitable partnerships exemplify a manufacturer's community engagement philosophy?
pending_qa.r: Warwick has sponsored Y Kids, a Bootle-based charity, for two to three years; the area ranks in the worst 6 percent of the UK for child literacy. Y Kids provides a bookstore and educational support helping children escape daily struggles while building reading and learning foundations. The charity presented Greg with a shirt inscribed with the phrase young people who believe that they can go on and make a difference, which embodies Warwick's approach to using its platform to affect local communities.
